name: Space Race
explanation: The United States and Soviet Russia extended their arms race to advancements in Space Exploration.
significance: The United States kept moving the goal post back until they literally reach the moon

name: Pentagon Papers
explanation: Classified papers about the vietnam war were leaked to the general public.
significance: Revealed a bunch of deceit and horrors of the Vietnam War.

name: Kent State Shootings
explanation: Also known as the Kent State Massacre, Ohio state guard killed 9 unarmed collage students.
significance: A bunch of peaceful protestors were shot protesting the Vietnam War.

name: My Lai Massacre
explanation: 347 to 504 unarmed civilians were killed by US soldiers
significance: U.S. Soldiers massacred a bunch of Vietnamese civilians.

name: Tonkin Gulf Crisis
explanation: Confrontation between the US and Vietnamese soldiers in the Tonkin Gulf
significance: Caused the U.S. to engage more directly in the Vietnam War.

name: Iran Hostage Crisis
explanation: American diplomats were held hostage in Iran, the U.S. has a standoff with Iran.
significance: Tanked the diplomatic relations between the US and Iran

name: Berlin Airlift
explanation: Soviet Russia blockaded West Berlin, so the U.S. airlifted the supplies in.
significance: Proved the soviets incompetent

name: Camp David Accords
explanation: 12 days of secret Peace talks between Israel and Egypt.
significance: led directly to the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty.

name: Israel's Creation
explanation: Israel was created to give the Jewish people their homeland back
significance: created at the end of ww2, sort of didn't work that well, didn't even have that much support.

name: Bay of Pigs Invasion
explanation: The US tried to invade the bay of pigs but was not given enough troops and supplies
significance: U.S. tried to attack Cuba and failed, raised tensions significantly.

name: Yalta Conference
explanation: Post-ww2 discussions of future.
significance: Meant to focus mainly on the rebuilding of war-torn countries in Europe.

name: Iran-Contra Affair
explanation: President secretly sold weapons to Iran without permission.
significance: Makes the president look bad.

name: Paris Peace Accord
explanation: Armistice in Vietnam war, American soldiers withdrawn.
significance: The US finally gave up on the war they were losing

name: War Powers Act
explanation: Signed by President Franklin D. Roosevelt that gave the President a large amount of authority over the US involvement in WWII.
significance: Increased executive power during WW2 just after Pearl Harbor.

name: Korean War
explanation: Proxy war to prevent the spread of communism in Korea.
significance: The reason that to this day North and South Korea are separate countries.

name: Vietnam War
explanation: Proxy war to prevent the spread of communism in Vietnam.
significance: absolute disaster for everyone involved and an enormous act of deceit and a breach of trust.

name: Perestroika
explanation: Political movement that sought political reform within the Soviet Union.
significance: lead to the end of the Soviet Union.

name: JFK Assassination
explanation: JFK was shot by Lee Harvey Oswald while riding in a car. His brother Robert Kennedy was shot some couple years after as well.
significance: The assassination was the first of four major assassinations during the 1960s in the United States

name: Cuban Missile Crisis
explanation: The US wanted Missiles out of Cuba and the Soviet Union wanted them out of Turkey.
significance: A time the world was almost destroyed because of a standoff over nuclear missiles placed in Cuba.

name: Formation of NATO
explanation: Established following WWII as a response to the cold war.
significance: 12 countries allied in one organization to protect against communism.

name: Formation of the Warsaw Pact
explanation: The Warsaw pact was made as a response to NATO.
significance: Designed to have a very similar organization among communist, soviet influenced countries.

name: Invasion of Cambodia
explanation: A series of military operations in east cambodia
significance: U.S. and South Vietnam invaded neutral Cambodia to find strategic positions to get at north Vietnam.

name: Division of Germany
explanation: Germany was split between the soviet controlled East and the French, English and American west.
significance: Berlin experienced much the same, even though it was in Russian territory.

name: Montgomery Bus Boycott
explanation: The day Rosa Parks was arrested, a bunch of people boycotted buses in Montgomery in protest of racial segregation.
significance: Produced a lot of media attention.

name: Voting Rights Act of 1965
explanation: Signed into law by Lyndon B. Johnson. Stopped voting discrimination based on race.
significance: Despite already being illegal, it was now extra illegal

name: Selma to Montgomery Marches
explanation: Black activists walked a very long distance through the south in a large group to protest lack of voting rights.
significance: They were attacked by police along the way.

name: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
explanation: MLK was assassinated at a hotel by James Earl Ray.
significance: A civil rights leader was murdered for believing in civil rights

name: Emmett Till Murder
explanation: Emmett Till was accused of offending a white women and lynched.
significance: His attackers were acquitted.

name: Watts Riots
explanation: Riot due to a black person resisting arrest, getting into a brawl, rumors spread that resulted in a riot.
significance: Riots were in response to police brutality.

name: Little Rock Nine
explanation: Nine black students enrolled in a white only school.
significance: landmark show of coming integration.

name: Fair Housing Act of 1968
explanation: Prohibited discrimination in the housing market.
significance: Despite there already being legislation to do that.

name: Freedom Rides
explanation: Large-scale bus trip protest of racial discrimination in bus terminals.
significance: They were attacked by mobs of racist people.

name: Bakke v. University of California
explanation: A white man was rejected in favor of minorities solely due to a racial quota and protested it.
significance: It highlighted the practice's potential flaws.

name: Memphis Sanitation Strike
explanation: Sanitation workers in Memphis protested poor treatment due to race and the death of 2 blacks.
significance: It did after much violence result in higher wages for the workers

name: Sit-ins
explanation: Occupying public spaces to protest racial segregation there, such as sitting in every seat in a restaurant and not buying anything.
significance: A form of non-violent protest used during the civil rights movement.

name: Birmingham campaigns
explanation: An effort to change discriminatory rules in Birmingham, Alabama.
significance: Used non-violent protests and paved the way for the civil rights acts.

name: Mississippi Freedom Summer
explanation: An effort to register massive numbers of black voters.
significance: It helped break down the decades of isolation and repression that had supported the Jim Crow system.

name: March on Washington
explanation: Large group of protestors did a protest in D.C.
significance: Site of the "I Have a Dream" speech.

name: Affirmative Action
explanation: Affirmative action was an effort to forcefully insert minorities into positions such as jobs or slots for students at colleges.
significance: This was the result of just waiting for thing to get better not really working out.

name: Miranda V. Arizona
explanation: The case that started the Miranda rights. a man was not told he had the right to remain silent and appealed based on that.
significance: A guilty man got away free because he was not properly informed.

name: Civil rights act of 1964
explanation: It outlaws discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, and national origin.
significance: Considered to be one of the most important landmark civil rights achievements in american history

name: Civil rights act of 1957
explanation: It was signed into law by President Eisenhower on September 9, 1957.
significance: Was trimmed town several times before being passed.

name: Formation of the Black Panther Party
explanation: founded by college students Bobby Seale and Huey P. Newton in October 1966
significance: Opposed the excessive force of the Oakland Police Department.
